gaps.sentence: The delegates arrived early ___ have time to network.
gaps.explanation: 'So as to + infinitive' = in order to, a formal purpose linker.

gaps.sentence: Bring a thermos ___ the tea tent closes at noon.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution against something happening.

gaps.sentence: Scarcely had she opened the letter ___ she burst into tears.
gaps.explanation: 'Scarcely... when' marks the immediate consequence of the first event.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.
'Firstly' opens a sequence of instructions; eventually/finally close one.

gaps.sentence: You can borrow the car ___ you fill the tank afterwards.
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' = only if, setting a requirement for permission.

gaps.sentence: He didn't whisper the news; ___, he announced it to the whole office.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' corrects the first statement with its opposite.

gaps.sentence: The lecture was dull; ___, the students stayed awake out of politeness.
